title: Fundamentos
intro: Cuatro unidades de repaso rápido. Si el diagnóstico te puso en A2 o más arriba, no necesitas hacerlas completas: revisa las notas de gramática, haz los ejercicios y sigue. Si te puso en A1, aquí está el piso sobre el que se construye todo lo demás — no te lo saltes.

units.title: Nice to meet you
units.titleEs: Verbo to be, pronombres y artículos
units.goal: presentarte, decir de dónde eres y a qué te dedicas.

grammar.title: The verb TO BE + articles
grammar.explanation:
«To be» es ser y estar a la vez. En inglés el sujeto NUNCA se omite: se dice «I am a student», nunca «Am a student».

En negativo se añade «not»; en pregunta el verbo se pone delante del sujeto.

Artículos: A antes de sonido consonántico (a car), AN antes de sonido vocálico (an engineer, an hour). Va por SONIDO, no por letra: «a university» lleva «a» porque suena «yu».

THE se usa cuando ya sabemos de qué hablamos. Con profesiones se usa a/an: «She is a doctor», no «She is doctor».
grammar.warning: Para la edad se usa BE, no HAVE: «I am 24», nunca «I have 24 years». Es el calco más común del español.

reading.title: A short introduction
reading.text:
Hello. My name is Erick Reyna. I'm twenty-four years old and I'm from Monterrey, in the north of Mexico.

I'm a mechatronics student at FIME. It's a big faculty and the classes are hard, but I'm happy there. My favourite subjects are electronics and control.

I'm not married. I live with my family. In my free time I play the guitar — I'm not very good yet, but I practise every week.

My English isn't perfect, but I'm working on it.

questions.explain: «I'm from Monterrey, in the north of Mexico».

questions.q: What does he do in his free time?
questions.explain: «In my free time I play the guitar».

exercises.explain: «university» suena «yu-», que es sonido consonántico → a. Va por sonido, no por letra.

answer: I am twenty four years old
exercises.explain: La edad va con BE, no con HAVE. «I have 24 years» es el calco típico del español.

exercises.audio: Hi, I'm Ana. I'm an engineer and I'm from Chile.
exercises.explain: «I'm an engineer». Fíjate en el «an» antes de sonido vocálico.
Posesivo antes del sustantivo: his name. «He's name» está mal.

writing.q: Preséntate: nombre, edad, de dónde eres, a qué te dedicas y qué haces en tu tiempo libre.
rubric: Puse el sujeto en todas las frases (nunca empecé con el verbo)
Usé la forma correcta de to be en cada persona
Dije mi edad con «I'm», no con «I have»
Usé a/an correctamente antes de la profesión
Llegué a 40 palabras
writing.model:
Hello. My name is Erick and I'm twenty-four years old. I'm from Monterrey, in the north of Mexico.

I'm a mechatronics student and I'm in my last semester. My favourite subjects are electronics and control systems. The classes are difficult, but they're interesting.

In my free time I play the guitar and I build small robots. I'm not very good at the guitar yet, but I practise every week.

units.title: Every day
units.titleEs: Presente simple y adverbios de frecuencia
units.goal: hablar de tu rutina y de lo que haces habitualmente.

grammar.title: Present simple
grammar.explanation:
Se usa para rutinas, hábitos y verdades generales.

Lo único difícil es la tercera persona (he/she/it): lleva -s. «I work» pero «He works».

En negativo y pregunta aparece el auxiliar DO / DOES, y entonces el verbo pierde la -s: «He doesn't work», nunca «He doesn't works».

Adverbios de frecuencia (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) van ANTES del verbo principal, pero DESPUÉS de to be: «I always study» / «I am always tired».

examples.en: I usually get up at six.
examples.es: Normalmente me levanto a las seis.

grammar.warning: «Never» ya es negativo: se dice «I never go», nunca «I don't never go».

vocab.example: She goes to work by bus.

reading.title: A normal Tuesday
reading.text:
I get up at six thirty, but I never get up immediately. I usually stay in bed for ten minutes and check my phone.

I have breakfast at seven and I leave the house at seven thirty. I don't drive — I take the bus, because parking at the university is impossible.

My first class starts at eight. On Tuesdays I have four classes and a lab session, so I finish at six in the evening. I sometimes stay longer if the lab isn't finished.

In the evening I study for about two hours. I don't watch much television. On Fridays I play the guitar with a friend, and at the weekend I usually sleep a lot.

questions.q: How does he go to the university?
questions.explain: «I don't drive — I take the bus».

questions.q: What time does he finish on Tuesdays?
questions.explain: «so I finish at six in the evening».

questions.q: What does he do on Fridays?
questions.explain: «On Fridays I play the guitar with a friend».

exercises.explain: Con doesn't, el verbo pierde la -s.
Pregunta con «she» → Does. Y el verbo va sin -s: «live».
El adverbio de frecuencia va antes del verbo principal.
Con to be, el adverbio va DESPUÉS: «is never».
El primer «do» es el auxiliar y el segundo el verbo. Significa «¿a qué te dedicas?».

exercises.audio: She usually starts at eight, but on Fridays she finishes early.

writing.q: Describe tu rutina de un día normal entre semana: a qué hora te levantas, qué haces, cómo te trasladas y qué haces en la noche. Usa al menos tres adverbios de frecuencia.
rubric: Puse -s en todos los verbos de tercera persona
Después de don't/doesn't dejé el verbo sin -s
Puse los adverbios de frecuencia antes del verbo principal
No usé doble negativo con «never»
Llegué a 50 palabras
writing.model:
I usually get up at six thirty during the week. I never get up before six, because I go to bed late.

I have breakfast at home and I take the bus to the university. I don't drive, because parking is very difficult there.

My classes start at eight and they finish at six. Sometimes I stay longer in the laboratory.

In the evening I study for two hours. I don't watch television, but I always play the guitar for a while before I sleep.

units.title: Where things are
units.titleEs: There is / there are, plurales y preposiciones de lugar
units.goal: describir un lugar y decir qué hay y dónde está.

grammar.title: There is / there are + prepositions
grammar.explanation:
THERE IS + singular o incontable. THERE ARE + plural.
«There is a problem.» «There are two problems.» «There is some water.»

En negativo: there isn't / there aren't. En pregunta: Is there…? / Are there…?

Plurales: se añade -s. Terminadas en -s, -sh, -ch, -x → -es (boxes, watches). Consonante + y → -ies (city / cities).

Irregulares que hay que saber: man/men, woman/women, child/children, person/people, foot/feet.

Preposiciones: IN (dentro), ON (sobre, tocando), UNDER (debajo), BEHIND (detrás), NEXT TO (junto a), BETWEEN (entre dos), IN FRONT OF (enfrente).

examples.en: There's a multimeter on the bench.
examples.es: Hay un multímetro sobre la mesa.

examples.en: There aren't any chairs in this room.
examples.es: No hay sillas en este cuarto.

examples.en: The box is under the table.
examples.es: La caja está debajo de la mesa.

examples.en: My laptop is next to the printer.
examples.es: Mi laptop está junto a la impresora.

grammar.warning: «There is» = hay (existe). «It is» = está (algo ya conocido). «There is a book on the table» presenta el libro; «It is on the table» habla de un libro del que ya hablábamos.

vocab.example: My desk is by the window.
There are books on the shelf.

reading.title: The electronics lab
reading.text:
Our electronics lab is on the second floor, next to the library. It isn't very big, but there is everything we need.

There are ten benches. On each bench there is an oscilloscope, a power supply and a soldering station. There are also two computers at the back, between the window and the door.

The components are in the drawers under the benches. There aren't any resistors in the small cabinet — those are in the storeroom behind the lab.

There are usually about twenty people in the lab in the afternoon. There's only one technician, so sometimes you wait.

questions.explain: «Our electronics lab is on the second floor, next to the library».

options: Between the window and the door
questions.explain: «two computers at the back, between the window and the door».
«There aren't any resistors in the small cabinet — those are in the storeroom».

exercises.q: There are five ___ in the room.
exercises.explain: «people» ya es el plural de person. «Peoples» significa «pueblos».

exercises.q: My phone is ___ the two books.
Traduce: «No hay sillas en el cuarto.»
answer: There aren't any chairs in the room
There are no chairs in the room
There aren't chairs in the room

exercises.answer: There is a lamp on the desk

exercises.audio: There's a printer behind the door and two boxes under the desk.
exercises.explain: «two boxes under the desk». La impresora es la que está detrás de la puerta.

writing.q: Describe tu cuarto, tu taller o tu escritorio: qué hay, cuántas cosas y dónde está cada una. Usa there is/there are y al menos cuatro preposiciones de lugar.
rubric: Usé «there is» con singular y «there are» con plural
Formé bien los plurales (incluidos los irregulares)
Usé al menos cuatro preposiciones de lugar distintas
No confundí «there is» (hay) con «it is» (está)
Llegué a 50 palabras
writing.model:
My workspace is small but organised. There is a desk next to the window and there are two shelves above it.

On the desk there is a laptop, a soldering station and a small lamp. My multimeter is between the lamp and the laptop, because I use it every day.

There are three boxes under the desk. The components are in those boxes, and there are more parts in the drawers behind me.

There aren't any chairs for visitors — there is only one chair, and it's mine.

units.title: Can you do it?
units.titleEs: Can / can't, imperativos y preguntas básicas
units.goal: hablar de lo que sabes hacer, dar instrucciones y hacer las preguntas más comunes.

grammar.title: Can + imperatives + question words
grammar.explanation:
CAN expresa habilidad y permiso. No lleva -s en tercera persona y va con el verbo en base: «She can drive», nunca «She cans» ni «She can to drive».

En negativo: can't (cannot). En pregunta: Can you…?

IMPERATIVO: es el verbo solo, sin sujeto. «Open the door.» «Don't touch that.» Se usa para instrucciones, avisos y manuales — por eso aparece tanto en textos técnicos.

PALABRAS INTERROGATIVAS: what (qué), where (dónde), when (cuándo), who (quién), why (por qué), how (cómo), how much (cuánto, incontable), how many (cuántos, contable), how long (cuánto tiempo).

examples.en: I can read datasheets, but I can't write fast in English.
examples.es: Puedo leer hojas de datos, pero no escribo rápido en inglés.

examples.en: Can you help me with this?

grammar.warning: Después de «can» nunca va «to»: «I can to help» está mal. Y en pregunta el orden es Can + sujeto + verbo: «Can you come?», no «You can come?».

reading.title: Quick start guide
reading.text:
QUICK START — READ FIRST

Before you begin, check the box. There are four items: the unit, a power cable, a USB cable and this guide. If something is missing, don't use the unit — contact support.

First, connect the power cable. Don't switch it on yet.

Then connect the USB cable to your computer. Wait ten seconds and press the button on the front. The light is orange at first. When it is green, the unit is ready.

You can use the unit without software, but you can't change the settings. To change them, install the application from our website.

Don't open the case. There are no user-serviceable parts inside.

questions.explain: «When it is green, the unit is ready».

questions.q: What can't you do without the software?
questions.explain: «you can use the unit without software, but you can't change the settings».

exercises.explain: Para precio se usa how much.
Imperativo negativo: Don't + verbo + objeto. Ojo con «switch on»: es separable, y con un pronombre el objeto va OBLIGATORIAMENTE en medio — «switch it on», nunca «switch on it».

exercises.audio: Press the button and wait. Don't open the case.

writing.q: Escribe instrucciones breves para usar algo que conoces bien (una herramienta, un aparato, un software). Usa imperativos afirmativos y negativos, y di qué se puede y qué no se puede hacer con él.
rubric: Usé el imperativo sin sujeto (Press…, no You press…)
Usé «Don't + verbo» para lo que no se debe hacer
Después de «can» puse el verbo en base, sin «to»
Las instrucciones están en orden lógico
Llegué a 50 palabras
writing.model:
HOW TO USE THE SOLDERING STATION

First, check the tip. If it is black, clean it with the sponge. Don't use sandpaper.

Switch on the station and set the temperature to 350 degrees. Wait two minutes. Don't touch the tip — it is very hot.

You can solder small components at this temperature, but you can't solder large ground planes. For those you can increase the temperature to 400.

When you finish, clean the tip again and switch off the station. Don't leave it on.
